newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - Enjoy dollar/yen rally while you can.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Enjoy dollar/yen rally while you can.

text.p: Nagging U.S. trade gap woes will soon put an end to the steady dollar/yen rally and send the rate lower through 1997, according to a Reuter poll.
A survey of over 20 analysts shows a consensus forecast for dollar/yen gradually fading toward 105 yen by the fourth quarter of 1997 from about 111 in the fourth quarter of 1996.
"The U.S. still runs a sizable current account deficit with Japan, which also has much lower inflation," said Sal Guatieri, senior economist at Bank of Montreal in Toronto.
"Those things will tend to raise the purchasing power of the yen compared to the dollar, over time," he added.
The mean forecast drops gradually from dollar/yen 111.06 to 105.36 yen over the next five quarters.
U.S. monetary policy poses a dilemma for currency rate handicappers, with analysts struggling to determine just how far, if at all, the Federal Reserve will boost rates.

"We believe the Fed will remain on hold over the next year, with a greater-than-average chance the U.S. economy will slow enough to move the unemployment rate up" to obviate the need for tighter credit, Guatieri said.
Dollar/yen late Wednesday stood at 112.25/35, just below the 112.39 level reached Tuesday, which represented at 33-month high.
